lines.text: Four Navy sailors confessed to the same murder. Not one of them did it.

Norfolk, Virginia, 1997. Michelle Moore-Bosko, a sailor's wife, is found murdered in her apartment. Within hours police land on her neighbor, a sailor: eleven overnight hours, a false polygraph claim, and he confesses before dawn.

Then his DNA comes back: no match. Police find another sailor. Then another. Four men confess. Every DNA test says no. Then the real killer writes from prison: Michelle got killed — guess who did that. Me. Ha, ha. His DNA matches everything. He acted alone.
The four stay convicted anyway — more than forty years combined — until a federal judge rules them actually innocent: no sane human being could find them guilty.
The detective who took those confessions? He went to federal prison too — for extortion in other cases. Follow for the cases they don't teach you.
